title: Normalized quotient ring equivalence and small-module lift
statement: For ell prime, E/Q_ell finite, an adic datum d on O_E and hd identifying d.ideal with the recorded uniformizer ideal, define the ring equivalence from PbcQuotient (pbcIntegralDatum ell E) n to O_E/d.ideal^(n+1) by integralCoefficientULift, ULift.down and equality of quotient ideals. Define the module lift by ModuleCat.uliftFunctor followed by scalar restriction along that equivalence. These are explicit constructions, with no existence assumption about module witnesses. The coefficient and normalized quotient conventions are [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-sfb-integral-completed-coefficient-transport].

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2), and Proposition 6.6.11; normalized coefficient presentations and localization of ringed sites.

proof.text: Compose the already uniquely normalized integralCoefficientULift with ULift.down and Ideal.quotEquivOfEq. The equation hd identifies the two quotient ideals. Compose module universe lift with restriction of scalars along this concrete ring equivalence. The representative formula is the choose_spec of integralCoefficientULift_exists followed by the defining quotient-equality map.

mathlib_searches.query: Perfect complexes over a large universe ring descend to small universe under a ring equivalence, with constant sheaf realization on slice sites
mathlib_searches.verdict: No exact match: generic derived-category representative APIs do not identify normalized finite coefficient presentations.
Use the full and faithful universe lift to descend bounded differentials.

mathlib_searches.verdict: Use Module.Finite.small and Shrink.linearEquiv for a direct finite-projective shrinking construction.
Exact restriction is available; these results do not compare finite scheme inverse image with normalized actual slices.

mathlib_searches.query: Constant sheaf of modules commutes with restricting scalars along a ring isomorphism and derived extension of scalars

from.place: The integral-lattice step: identify the large residue ring with the small uniformizer quotient before shrinking finite-projective terms.

lean.statement:
abbrev integralResidueQuotientLift
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (d : AdicCoefficientDatum (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))
    (hd : d.ideal = Ideal.span {Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E}) (n : ℕ) :
    ModuleCat.{u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1)) ⥤
      ModuleCat.{u + 1} (PbcQuotient (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n)
